audits.title: When urinary catheters stay too long: the hidden link between constipation, prolonged indwelling urinary catheterisation and urinary tract infections in neurosurgical inpatients.
audits.standard: Guidelines on urinary catheterisation; trial without catheter within 24 hours
audits.setting: National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, London

cycle1.result: 94% UTI rate with indwelling catheters; indwelling catheter use 25.6% in 2020; TWOC within 24 h 3% in 2021.

audits.intervention: Nurse-led trial without catheter, early physiotherapy, bowel care and constipation prevention, tailored protocols, staff education and clinical champions.

cycle2.result: Indwelling catheter use fell to 11% by end-2023; CAUTI fell to 45.5% by 2024; TWOC within 24 h rose to 93% in 2024.

audits.other_findings: Three sequential audits and six linked QIPs over five years; gains sustained with quarterly education and biannual data review.
audits.citation: Tariq K, Vankipuram S, Khawari S, Giannis T, Kakar V, Alexandris C, et al.. When urinary catheters stay too long: the hidden link between constipation, prolonged indwelling urinary catheterisation and urinary tract infections in neurosurgical inpatients. Br J Neurosurg. 2026. doi:10.1080/02688697.2026.2677912. PMID: 42226604.

audits.title: Preventing pediatric catheter-associated urinary tract infections utilizing urinary catheter Kamishibai cards (K-cards).
audits.setting: Free-standing children's hospital, hospital-wide (Boston Children's Hospital)

cycle1.result: Bundle element 'medical discussion of need for the urinary catheter' 88%; overall bundle reliability 84%

audits.intervention: Kamishibai card (K-card) rounding: weekly standardised audit questions with real-time feedback to nurses

cycle2.result: Discussion of need for catheter 94% (P = .01); overall bundle reliability stable at 84%; CAUTI rate fell (incidence rate ratio 0.38, 95% CI 0.15-0.93)

audits.other_findings: 826 K-card audits were performed in total.
audits.citation: Lehane R, Svensson C, Ormsby JA, Yuen JC, Priebe GP, Sandora TJ, et al.. Preventing pediatric catheter-associated urinary tract infections utilizing urinary catheter Kamishibai cards (K-cards). Am J Infect Control. 2023;51(8):919-925. doi:10.1016/j.ajic.2022.11.019. PMID: 36463976.

audits.title: Rounding and Quick Access Education to Reduce Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections.
audits.standard: Catheter maintenance bundle; aim to reduce CAUTI rates by 75%
audits.setting: Two inpatient surgical units, tertiary medical centre (Madigan Army Medical Center)
audits.intervention: QR code with prevention resources, educational handouts, and champion rounding with bundle adherence audits

cycle2.result: CAUTI 0.64 per 1000 catheter days; maintenance bundle compliance 67%

audits.citation: Garcia DM, Makic MBF, Casey K. Rounding and Quick Access Education to Reduce Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections. Clin Nurse Spec. 2023;37(3):117-123. doi:10.1097/nur.0000000000000741. PMID: 37058702.
